text: Ten fictional nonprofit programme passages across varied genres, each with eight quote variants for citation-checker testing.

passages.source_passage: By the midpoint of the Little Steps Playgroup Network's 2022-2025 grant, 46 of the planned 60 playgroups were meeting weekly in village halls across the Marlow Valley. Average attendance reached 18 children per session, up from 11 at baseline. Caregivers reported no significant cost barriers, although three groups lost their venues during the 2023 rains. Facilitators completed the full training cycle in 83 percent of sites. The evaluation team found that books and toys were rarely rotated between groups, and that no site kept written records of child progress before March 2023. Recommendations focus on shared materials and simple record keeping.

variants.whitespace_case: FACILITATORS completed the full training  cycle in 83 percent of sites.
variants.punctuation: Caregivers reported no significant cost barriers although three groups lost their venues during the 2023 rains.
variants.changed_quantity: Facilitators completed the full training cycle in 38 percent of sites.
variants.added_negation: 46 of the planned 60 playgroups were not meeting weekly in village halls across the Marlow Valley
variants.removed_negation: Caregivers reported significant cost barriers, although three groups lost their venues during the 2023 rains
variants.reordered: although their venues lost three groups during the 2023 rains
variants.paraphrase: Sessions now draw an average of 18 children, compared with 11 when the project began.

passages.source_passage: Volunteer trainers at the Harbourview Skills Centre support young people aged 16 to 24 through a 12-week course in basic carpentry and electrical wiring. Please arrive at least 15 minutes before each session so that tools can be counted and checked. Never allow a trainee to use a power saw before he or she has completed the safety induction, which takes two hours. Do not mark trainees down for arriving late on public transport days; the centre does not penalise lateness caused by bus delays. In 2024, 71 percent of graduates found paid work within six months, and we hope you will help us keep that figure rising.

passages.source_passage: The Luna Verde Scholarship Programme has supported 312 girls in lower secondary school across four municipalities in western Honduras since January 2021. At the midpoint review, 89 percent of scholars remained enrolled, compared with 64 percent of a comparison group. Families did not receive cash directly; payments went to schools for fees, uniforms and transport passes. The evaluators found that mentoring sessions were held twice a month in most clusters, but no cluster offered mentoring during the harvest season. Pregnancy remained the main reason for dropout, accounting for roughly one third of withdrawals. The review recommends extending support to upper secondary level.

passages.source_passage: Since mid-2022 the Kibanda District Health Programme has deployed 240 community health workers, each responsible for about 100 households in the Lake Rukwa catchment. By the review date, 92 percent had completed the initial 10-day course, and 78 percent had received at least one supervisory visit in the previous quarter. Supplies were not consistently available: stock-outs of malaria rapid tests affected 14 of 31 health posts. Workers are unpaid volunteers, and the programme has no plan to introduce salaries before 2026. Even so, referral rates for children under five rose from 120 to 205 per month, which district officers described as encouraging.

passages.source_passage: This year the Dawn Reader Network ran evening literacy classes in 38 locations, up from 29 in 2023. A total of 1,150 adults enrolled, and 68 percent of them were women. Learners who attended at least three sessions a week gained an average of two reading levels. We did not meet our target of certifying 900 learners by December, mainly because examination dates were postponed by the regional board. No class closed for lack of a teacher, though six relied on volunteers who had received only five days of preparation. We thank the Alder Trust for its continued support.

passages.source_passage: The Saltmarsh Coast is home to roughly 54,000 people living in 19 fishing villages, most within two kilometres of the shoreline. Cyclone Ines in 2019 killed 37 residents, and investigators concluded that many deaths could have been avoided had warnings arrived earlier. At that time the villages had no siren system, and the national alert reached households only through radio, which many fishers do not carry at sea. Since then the Coastal Readiness Alliance has installed sirens in seven villages. This proposal seeks funds to extend coverage to the remaining twelve villages by 2027 and to train 150 local volunteers.

variants.removed_negation: the national alert reached households only through radio, which many fishers do carry at sea
variants.reordered: investigators concluded that many warnings could have been avoided had deaths arrived earlier
variants.paraphrase: In those days the villages lacked sirens and relied on radio alerts alone, which fishers out at sea often could not receive.

passages.source_passage: Board members asked for a short update on the Mwanga Home Care Programme. As of 30 June, our 42 caregivers were visiting 560 clients each month, and 91 percent of clients on antiretroviral treatment reported no missed doses in the previous four weeks. We did not reach the target of 600 clients, because two caregivers resigned in April and replacements have not yet completed training. Transport remains the largest cost, at about 38 percent of the budget. No client has been refused a visit because of distance, but travel times in the northern ward are now over three hours. We will present a revised route plan at the September meeting.

passages.source_passage: This session introduces farmers to sorghum and cowpea varieties that tolerate dry spells of up to 21 days. Begin by showing the two demonstration plots planted on 10 October, one with improved seed and one with local seed. Do not tell farmers which plot is which until they have made their own observations. Remind them that improved seed is not a guarantee against crop failure; it simply lowers the risk. Last season, 64 farmers in the Dunmore cluster adopted at least one variety, and about 45 percent of them saved seed for planting this year. Allow 90 minutes for the session, including questions.

passages.source_passage: The Tamarind Hills Farmer Field School Network enrolled 1,420 smallholders in 71 schools between 2021 and 2023. Participants applied an average of four recommended practices, such as row planting and compost making, compared with just over one practice among non-participants. Maize yields rose by 27 percent on participating plots, although the difference was not statistically significant in the two driest districts. Women made up 52 percent of members but only 19 percent of facilitators. The evaluators did not find evidence that the schools reached the poorest households, who often lacked time to attend weekly sessions. A revised targeting strategy is due by March 2025.

passages.source_passage: This update covers the Rivermead Borehole and Latrine Project for the quarter ending 31 March. Crews drilled nine boreholes, bringing the total to 34, and six of the nine now have working hand pumps. Three sites are not yet operational because the pump parts shipped from the capital have not arrived. Households built 212 latrines with our subsidy, but fewer than half have handwashing stations. Water committees did not collect fees at 11 sites, so repairs there depend on emergency funds. The finance report shows the project is 8 percent under budget, and no staff were laid off. A site visit is planned for June.
